## Sources found

### In-situ chamber fluxes, all of them east of the Danish straits

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-HYLEN">**Hylén et al. (2025)**, *In situ-measured benthic fluxes of dissolved inorganic phosphorus in the Baltic Sea* (Earth System Science Data), publish [498](../SOURCES.md#F-a53276a940) DIP fluxes measured in situ with benthic chamber landers at [59](../SOURCES.md#F-a53276a940) stations between 2001 and 2021, with bottom-water oxygen, sediment organic carbon and sediment type beside them. The data are one file, `BalticSeaInSituFluxDIP_v3.xlsx`, in Zenodo record `17465937`, under the Creative Commons Attribution licence.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-HYLEN "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-HYLEN-WEST">They do not count the Kattegat and the Belt Sea, west of the Arkona Basin, as part of the Baltic Sea, and the westernmost subbasin they group is the Arkona and Bornholm Basin, so no station of theirs lies in the Kattegat or the Belts.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-HYLEN-WEST "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-HYLEN-PATH">A chamber lander incubating a patch of bed is a different instrument, quantity and operator from the CTD sonde - the authors are at the University of Gothenburg, GEOMAR and elsewhere, not Danish monitoring - so it is a production path separate from the CTD, ocean colour and Secchi.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-HYLEN-PATH "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### Others found

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-FR483">**NERI Technical Report `483`** (Fossing et al. 2004) sets up an oxygen and nutrient flux model for Aarhus Bay. Its constants were set by comparing the model's stationary state with a year's mean measurements from the HAV90 programme in Aarhus Bay, and it cites that programme's reports on the sea floor's oxygen uptake (Gundersen et al. 1995) and nitrogen cycling (Lomstein and Blackburn 1992).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-FR483 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-AL561">**AL561** (GEOMAR, 2021): benthic landers and cores at high-accumulation sites in the Skagerrak and Kattegat; the chamber record at station `AL561_17-1` lists phosphate and ammonium among its measured nutrients, and the source register records the cruise's stations reaching from the Kattegat to the Skagerrak, several of them nearer Sweden or Norway.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-AL561 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-TA14">**NOVA teknisk anvisning `kap. 14`** (1998) specifies light and dark incubations of sediment cores for the fluxes of oxygen, ortho-phosphate, nitrate, nitrite, ammonium, urea and silicate, on type areas only.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-TA14 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-SR323">**DCE's SR323** tabulates the internal and external load of DIN and DIP for Roskilde, Odense, Horsens and Ringkøbing Fjord by three-month period from summer 1999 to spring 2000, credited to unpublished data by H. It cites Kerteminde Fjord, where in 1991–1992 the sediment's release made up [65](../SOURCES.md#F-ce5a27839b)% and [70](../SOURCES.md#F-ce5a27839b)% of the total N and P load.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-SR323 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-SR323-DATA">The measurements behind the table were not found in any reachable dataset.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-SR323-DATA "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Does this break the model-as-datum residual, or inherit it?

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-RESID">Internal loading inferred as what a mass balance leaves over is model-as-datum by construction. FR483 is a local instance: a model of Aarhus Bay whose constants were fitted to a year's measured means.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-RESID "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-DIPFORM">The **DIP-seasonality form breaks it.** It sets one directly observed quantity (summer minus winter ortho-phosphate near the bed) against another (loss on ignition and iron-adsorbed P at the same position). No budget is closed, nothing is a remainder. The price is that it is **weak**: a summer DIP rise over organic-rich bed is equally consistent with water-column regeneration co-located with it, since deposition drives both. It can *falsify* the benthic signature - no covariance means [A7](../openproblems/A7.md "Sediment nutrient regeneration") leaves no mark at station resolution - but a positive result does not isolate the bed.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-DIPFORM "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-CHAMBERFORM">The **chamber form breaks it completely** and is the only thing that isolates the bed; the in-situ chamber fluxes found for Danish inner waters are one cruise's.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-CHAMBERFORM "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-JANFEB">**The January–February sampling is why the residual keeps reappearing.** The pool is measured once a year, in winter; the release is claimed for summer. With one annual observation the summer drawdown *cannot* be a difference of two measurements, so anyone wanting a number must infer it. The programme design forces model-as-datum here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-JANFEB "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Smallest unblocking thing

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-S1">**One fetch.** `Emne_12_19` (Sedimentkemi): [39](../SOURCES.md#F-84464ace67) stations ever, and it fixes how many positions the test can have. `scripts/fetch_oda.py` has no entry for it: its `TOPICS` already carry the water chemistry `Emne_10_11`, and its argument parser accepts only those keys, so it is one entry more, the node id already recorded in `data/manual/data_sources.json`. Set an explicit period - the portal's station list is filtered by the period set, and returns the current network without one.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-S1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-S2">**Check the join before designing anything.** Count stations carrying *both* a sediment core and ≥[5](../SOURCES.md#F-c16a638fd5) years of monthly DIP within [2](../SOURCES.md#F-f945894f46) km. If fewer than [10](../SOURCES.md#F-4058d83d39) do, the armchair classification is wrong and [A7](../openproblems/A7.md "Sediment nutrient regeneration") is a measurement gap in both forms. Stating this in advance is the point.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-S2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-S3">**The measurement.** Sample the existing sediment stations **twice**, late February and late September, instead of once in winter. That change turns the summer release from a residual into a difference of two measured pools, at whatever station count is already funded. Then: one chamber deployment in the Kattegat, the Belts or a Danish fjord, where no chamber flux was found.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-S3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What a completed test would and would not license

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-WOULD">**Would.** Whether near-bed phosphate seasonality covaries with bed organic content across positions, as a coefficient with its qualifiers.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-WOULD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-OQ-A7-WOULDNOT">**Would not.** Any share, tonnage or "internal loading accounts for n%": that is a mass balance and this is not one. Nor anything about Danish inner waters from the Zenodo data, whose basins the paper defines as excluding the Kattegat and the Belt Sea - carrying them westward would be the aggregation error this project audits elsewhere.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-OQ-A7-WOULDNOT "What this claim rests on")</sup>
